documents.title: 中央网信办深入开展“清朗·整治AI技术滥用”专项行动第一阶段工作
documents.issuing_body: 中央网络安全和信息化委员会办公室 / Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a progress report on Phase 1 of the 'Qinglang: Rectification of AI Technology Abuse' campaign launched April 2025. The document describes enforcement actions already taken and outlines Phase 2 plans focusing on AI-generated misinformation and vulgar content. Penalties are referenced prospectively ('形成处置处罚规范') but not yet fully specified. The document functions as both a regulatory guidance report and an enforcement action summary. Safety requirements are inferred from described platform actions rather than explicit legal mandates in this document.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document centers on maintaining a 'clean and healthy online ecosystem' (清朗网络生态) and combating AI misuse such as deepfakes harming public rights, missing content labels misleading the public, and AI-generated rumors. The primary justification is social order and online environment governance rather than economic competitiveness or existential risk. Rights protection (侵犯公众权益) and consumer safety are secondary concerns explicitly mentioned.

documents.title: 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室、工业和信息化部、公安部、国家广播电视总局
documents.implementation_notes: Document mandates explicit and implicit labeling of AI-generated synthetic content. Explicit labels must appear at specific positions in text, audio, image, video, and virtual scenes. Implicit labels (e.g., digital watermarks, file metadata) are encouraged. Distribution platforms must check metadata and apply appropriate labels. Prohibition on malicious removal or falsification of labels. Specific penalties not detailed in the provided text excerpt.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around maintaining social public order and protecting citizens' lawful rights through mandatory labeling of AI-generated content. The stated goals are to 'protect citizens, legal persons and other organizations' lawful rights' and 'maintain social public interests,' indicating a social stability and rights protection framing rather than existential risk or economic competition.

documents.title: 《国家药监局关于“人工智能+药品监管”的实施意见》政策解读
documents.issuing_body: 国家药品监督管理局 (National Medical Products Administration)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a policy interpretation/reading document accompanying the main implementation opinion on 'AI + Drug Regulation' issued by NMPA. It outlines a 5-10 year roadmap (targets for 2030 and 2035) for integrating AI into drug regulatory processes including review/approval, inspection, risk monitoring, and administrative services. AI is explicitly positioned as auxiliary ('辅助型定位'). Enforcement mechanisms are primarily administrative/supervisory rather than punitive. The document encourages industry digital transformation especially for high-risk categories like blood products and TCM injections.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance in drug regulation as an opportunity to modernize and enhance regulatory capabilities through technology integration. The core reasoning is enabling smarter, more efficient regulation rather than mitigating risks from AI itself. Secondary framing includes consumer/public safety through improved drug lifecycle oversight and economic competitiveness via industry digital transformation.

documents.title: 新一代人工智能伦理规范
documents.issuing_body: 国家新一代人工智能治理专业委员会 (National New Generation AI Governance Professional Committee)
documents.implementation_notes: This document is an ethics guideline (伦理规范) rather than binding law. It provides normative guidance for all actors in the AI lifecycle (managers, developers, suppliers, users) but does not specify legal penalties or mandatory enforcement mechanisms. Binding force is ambiguous; treated as regulatory guidance given the issuing body's authority, but closer to a soft-law instrument.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around protecting individual rights and human dignity—privacy, autonomy, informed consent, anti-discrimination, and fairness. The six core ethical requirements center on human welfare, equity, privacy protection, and human control, reflecting a fundamental rights framing. Secondary frames include social stability (harmonious human-machine relations, sustainable development, social justice) and consumer/public safety (controllability, accountability mechanisms).

documents.title: 新一代人工智能治理原则——发展负责任的人工智能
documents.issuing_body: 国家新一代人工智能治理专业委员会 (National New Generation AI Governance Professional Committee)
documents.implementation_notes: This document is a high-level principles framework (治理原则) issued by an advisory committee, not binding legislation. It outlines eight principles for responsible AI development but does not specify enforcement mechanisms or penalties. It functions as a strategy/guidance statement encouraging voluntary adherence and international cooperation.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's eight principles foreground rights-based concerns—privacy, fairness, non-discrimination, informed consent, and human dignity—as the primary justification for AI governance. While innovation and social harmony are also present, the explicit articulation of individual rights (知情权、选择权), prohibition of bias and discrimination, and data protection norms make fundamental rights the dominant frame.

documents.title: 国家互联网信息办公室关于《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法（征求意见稿）》公开征求意见的通知
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a draft regulation (征求意见稿) open for public comment until 2024-10-14. It is not yet in force. Enforcement penalties are not specified in this excerpt but would likely be governed by referenced parent regulations. The document mandates explicit AI-generated content labeling and encourages implicit watermarking. Applies to service providers offering services to domestic users in China.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's stated rationale centers on regulating AI-generated synthetic content labeling to 'maintain national security and social public interest' and protect citizens' legal rights. The emphasis on preventing deception through mandatory disclosure of AI-generated content reflects a social stability framing, with secondary concerns about consumer protection and individual rights.

documents.title: 专家解读｜深化生成合成内容标识治理，完善人工智能技术安全体系
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China)
documents.implementation_notes: This is an expert interpretation article published by CAC accompanying the '人工智能生成合成内容标识办法' (AI-Generated Content Labeling Measures) and companion national mandatory standard. The document itself is commentary/guidance rather than the primary regulatory instrument. It references mandatory labeling requirements for AI-generated content across modalities (text, image, audio, video) including both explicit (visible) and implicit (metadata) labeling. Binding force derives from the underlying '标识办法' which is described as a mandatory standard.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance around preventing misinformation, technical abuse, and protecting network ecosystem security—core social stability concerns. It emphasizes content labeling to maintain information order, user awareness, and traceable/trustworthy AI. Secondary frames include consumer/public safety (user rights, transparency) and innovation enablement (balancing regulation with industry development).

documents.title: 人工智能安全治理框架
documents.issuing_body: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a framework document (V1.0) issued by TC260 in September 2024, implementing the Global AI Governance Initiative. It is structured as a standards/guidance document rather than binding legislation, though it references compliance with existing laws and regulations. Enforcement mechanisms are largely implied through reference to 'competent authorities' rather than explicitly specified. The document covers the full AI lifecycle and addresses both developers, service providers, and users including a separate section for critical sector users. Registration/filing (登记备案) requirements for high-compute or sector-specific AI systems suggest emerging binding elements, but the document itself functions as a governance framework and guidelines document.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document repeatedly foregrounds national sovereignty, ideological security, and state security interests as primary justifications for AI governance. Risks are classified partly by domain—including a 'cognitive domain' explicitly referencing 'cognitive warfare' and foreign interference in domestic affairs—and supply chain security concerns are framed around hostile foreign technology controls. The framework explicitly aims to 'safeguard national sovereignty, security and development interests.' While social stability, rights protection, and safety concerns are present, the overarching governance rationale is national security.

documents.title: 国家人工智能产业综合标准化体系建设指南
documents.issuing_body: 中华人民共和国工业和信息化部
documents.implementation_notes: This is a standardization framework/guideline document (指南) for China's AI industry standards system (2024 edition). It sets targets to develop 50+ national/industry standards and 20+ international standards by 2026. It covers the full AI industry chain from infrastructure to applications, with safety/governance standards as one of seven pillars. No explicit penalties or binding enforcement mechanisms are specified; compliance is encouraged through guidance and promotion activities. The document appears issued by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) consistent with similar documents.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around building China's AI standardization system to drive high-quality industrial development and global competitiveness. The stated goals emphasize seizing the first-mover advantage in AI industry development, expanding market scale, participating in international standards, and enabling new industrialization. Safety and governance standards appear as one component among seven, subordinate to the overarching economic and industrial development framing.

documents.title: 关于加强互联网信息服务算法综合治理的指导意见
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China) et al. (9 ministries)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a guidance document (指导意见) jointly issued by 9 ministries. It sets a 3-year goal to establish algorithm governance mechanisms. The document calls for creating regulations and standards as follow-up measures, indicating that binding legal rules are anticipated but not yet fully in place. Civil penalties are implied by references to punishing violations but specific penalty amounts are not stated in this document.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames algorithm governance as necessary to maintain correct information order, ideological security, market order, and social order. The central concern is preventing algorithms from disrupting social stability, spreading harmful content, or undermining ideological alignment. Secondary concerns include protecting netizens' rights (fundamental_rights), supporting domestic algorithm innovation to build competitive strength (innovation_enablement), and maintaining ideological/national security.

documents.title: 互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China), 工业和信息化部, 公安部, 国家市场监督管理总局
documents.implementation_notes: This regulation governs algorithm recommendation services in China, covering personalized push, ranking, filtering, and decision-scheduling algorithms. It establishes a tiered registration/filing (备案) system for providers with public opinion influence or social mobilization capacity. Requirements include algorithmic transparency to users, user opt-out mechanisms, content labeling for AI-generated content, and periodic safety assessments. Penalties range from warnings and fines (10,000–100,000 RMB) to suspension of service updates and criminal liability for serious violations.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames algorithm recommendation governance as necessary to maintain social order and uphold 'socialist core values,' prevent disruption to economic and social order, and suppress harmful information. The recurring emphasis on 'social public interest,' 'social mobilization capability,' 'public opinion attributes,' and preventing content that disturbs social order places social stability as the dominant frame. Secondary frames include fundamental rights (user transparency, opt-out rights, protections for minors, elderly, and workers), consumer/public safety (fraud prevention, minor protection, anti-addiction), and national security (explicit mention of national security protection).

documents.title: 专家解读｜人工智能拟人化互动服务的制度指引
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China)
documents.implementation_notes: This document is an expert interpretation (专家解读) of the 'Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic Interactive Services of Artificial Intelligence' published by CAC. It is not the regulation itself but an authoritative commentary explaining the regulation's intent and requirements. The underlying 办法 (Measures) would be binding; this interpretive piece reflects that binding content. The document focuses on AI companion/emotional interaction services, covering minors protection, addiction prevention, crisis intervention, and data privacy.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI anthropomorphic interaction risks in terms of social stability—specifically the erosion of real human relationships, emotional dependency, social isolation, and harm to vulnerable groups (minors, elderly, psychologically fragile individuals). The governance rationale centers on preserving the social fabric and healthy human relationships, with secondary attention to consumer/public safety (crisis intervention, self-harm prevention) and fundamental rights (privacy, personal data protection), while also affirming innovation enablement as a co-equal policy goal.

documents.title: 人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China)
documents.implementation_notes: This regulation specifically targets anthropomorphic/emotional AI interaction services (拟人化互动服务), explicitly excluding customer service, Q&A, work assistants, and educational tools without continuous emotional interaction. It was jointly issued by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS, and SAMR. The document type is formally an interim administrative measure (暂行办法) which is binding regulation in China's legal system. Notable focus on minor protection, psychological health, and emotional dependency risks.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI anthropomorphic interaction risks in terms of social stability: preventing emotional dependency, protecting minors, curbing manipulation, and maintaining socialist core values and social order. Secondary framings include fundamental rights (personal information, privacy, user autonomy) and consumer/public safety (mental health interventions, crisis detection). National security appears as a baseline concern (prohibiting content harming state security) but is not the organizing logic.

documents.title: 《人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法》答记者问
documents.issuing_body: 国家网信办、国家发展改革委、工业和信息化部、公安部、市场监管总局
documents.implementation_notes: This is a press Q&A document explaining the Interim Measures for Management of Anthropomorphic Interaction Services Using AI, jointly issued by five agencies. The measures take effect 2026-07-15. Scope is limited to persistent emotional interaction services; excludes customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education tools without persistent emotional interaction. Key focus areas: minors protection (under-14 requires guardian consent), elderly user safeguards, algorithm filing/registration, sandbox testing platform, and user dependency intervention obligations.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around protecting users—especially minors and the elderly—from harms such as emotional manipulation, addiction, self-harm, and privacy violations. The detailed provisions on intervention obligations, dependency warnings, and crisis response reinforce a consumer/public safety dominant frame. Secondary frames include fundamental rights (data rights, privacy, personal dignity), social stability (prohibitions on content threatening state security and social order), and innovation enablement (sandbox platforms, encouraging R&D).

documents.title: 国家网信办等五部门联合公布《人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法》_中央网络安全和信息化委员会办公室
documents.issuing_body: 国家网信办、国家发展改革委、工业和信息化部、公安部、市场监管总局
documents.implementation_notes: 《办法》规定安全评估、算法备案制度，并指导推动人工智能沙箱安全服务平台建设；对拟人化互动服务实行包容审慎和分类分级监管。
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI humanized interaction services governance primarily around social stability—protecting minors, the elderly, and public order, and preventing ethical deviations and harms to social wellbeing. It also emphasizes national security (prohibiting content that undermines state power), fundamental rights (personal information protection, user rights), and innovation enablement (encouraging development alongside regulation).

documents.title: 互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China), 工业和信息化部, 公安部
documents.implementation_notes: Regulations cover 'deep synthesis' (deepfake/generative AI) services including text, image, audio, video, and virtual scene generation. Key obligations include mandatory watermarking/labeling of synthetic content, real-name authentication of users, security assessment for biometric editing tools, and registration for services with public opinion influence. Enforcement references existing cybersecurity and public security laws for specific penalty amounts.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames deep synthesis governance as necessary to maintain social order, public morality, and correct political/public opinion orientation. It repeatedly emphasizes preventing disinformation, protecting 'social public interests,' and maintaining 'economic and social order.' National security is a strong secondary frame, with explicit prohibitions on content harming national security and requirements for security assessments on content involving national image. Fundamental rights (personal information, biometric data protection) and consumer/public safety (anti-fraud, labeling requirements) are also present.

documents.title: 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法
documents.issuing_body: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China) et al.
documents.implementation_notes: Interim measures applying to generative AI services provided to the public within China. Classified/tiered supervision approach indicated. Research and internal use not covered. Foreign providers offering services into China are also subject to these rules.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's primary governance rationale centers on maintaining social order and ideological stability—prohibiting content that undermines state power, social stability, or socialist values. National security appears as a closely related secondary concern. The document also strongly promotes innovation and self-reliance in AI development, and addresses individual rights such as personal information protection.

documents.title: Measures for Artificial Intelligence Meteorological Application Services
documents.issuing_body: China Meteorological Administration (CMA) and Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)
documents.implementation_notes: This is described as the first departmental regulation in China to promote and regulate AI in a segmented area, and the first legal standard on AI meteorological application services among WMO members. It covers algorithm registration, security assessments, content labeling, safety review, cyber security, data security, and complaint reporting. Details on penalties are not provided in the available text.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance in meteorology as enabling healthy and well-organized development, balancing innovation promotion with governance. The stated aim is to encourage and promote AI application services while managing potential hazards, with explicit policy support for R&D and application scenarios. Safety and security measures are secondary to the innovation promotion goal.

documents.title: 国务院关于印发新一代人工智能发展规划的通知
documents.implementation_notes: This is China's 2017 New Generation AI Development Plan (新一代人工智能发展规划), a high-level national strategy document issued by the State Council. It is primarily a strategy/roadmap document with three-phase goals to 2030. While it directs ministries to develop laws, regulations, and standards, it does not itself constitute binding law. Safety and governance provisions are largely aspirational with implementation delegated to future rulemaking. The document explicitly calls for future development of AI laws, ethics frameworks, safety monitoring systems, and standards—meaning most enforcement mechanisms are anticipated rather than operative at time of publication. Confidence scores for enforcement mechanisms are conservative given this forward-looking character.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document overwhelmingly frames AI governance through the lens of economic competitiveness and national strategic advantage. The core motivation is to seize a first-mover advantage in AI, build internationally competitive industries, and drive economic growth. National security is a strong secondary frame, with explicit references to maintaining strategic initiative in international AI competition and supporting national defense. Social stability, labor transition, and innovation enablement also appear as secondary concerns.
